A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Show-o research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and all supplementary material support comparison. V1 ends with references; v5 adds Appendices A.1 and A.2.

before.justification: V1 reports original understanding and generation benchmarks, representation ablations, and qualitative image and video-keyframe results.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds data-scale and resolution experiments, updated benchmark scores, and revised qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, QK normalization, image tokenizer, omni-attention, combined next-token/masked-token objectives, and MaskGIT-based generation remain substantively unchanged. V5 expands inference and masking documentation; its larger training corpus, budget, and image resolution do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V5 substantially expands actual training sources by incorporating DataComp, COYO700M, and an internal high-quality image-text collection alongside the public sources used in v1. The evaluation benchmarks and task families remain unchanged; no additional evaluation domain is demonstrated.

E2.justification: V5 adds DreamLLM-7B to the understanding and MSCOCO comparisons in Tables 1 and 2. It also adds Chameleon-7B to GenEval Table 3; Chameleon-34B already appeared in the understanding comparison. The other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Beyond v1's training schedule, v5 reports 500K further steps on approximately 2.0B image-text pairs, another 500K steps at 512×512 resolution, and internal-data fine-tuning. Table 4 compares corpus sizes and resolutions. The sampling study changes from 2/8/16 steps at 256×256 to 5/25/50 at 512×512 and uses different guidance scales.

E4.justification: V5 Table 4 adds substantive ablations testing data scale and image resolution across six understanding benchmarks. V1's encoder, representation, and unified-pretraining ablations remain unchanged as v5 Table 5. Sampling/guidance examples and failure cases are revised, including the difficulty of generating appropriate skis for individual people.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V5's token-confidence descriptions concern decoding, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces default Show-o's MME score of 948.4 with 1097.2 and VQAv2(test) score of 59.3 with 69.4; Table 3 replaces GenEval overall 0.53 with 0.68. These accompany changed training configurations, not established same-setting gains. V5 also adds scaling results and replaces qualitative outputs. Show-o's FID remains 9.24, and the original representation-ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: V1 briefly invokes the connection between masked generation and discrete diffusion. V5 Section 3 adds transition distributions, absorbing-uniform corruption, an ELBO, and an alternative lower bound; Appendix A.1 supplies a detailed derivation attributed to Zhang et al. This is substantial mathematical content, although the new exposition contains conditional-independence and transition-normalization inconsistencies.

C1.justification: V5 expands the introduction's stated analytical contribution from representation choices to include dataset scale and image resolution. The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims about unified autoregressive/diffusion modeling, competitive performance, and supported applications.

C2.justification: V5 interprets the new scaling results as evidence that discrete-token understanding benefits from more alignment data and more image tokens. It also explicitly identifies incorrect object belongings, such as skis, as a failure condition. Earlier explanations of representation differences, data limitations, and FID distribution mismatch remain.

D1.justification: New Section 4.4 and Appendix A.2 document parallel token sampling, confidence-based retention, remasking counts and thresholds, and final decoding. V5 also specifies additional training stages and budgets. These substantially expand procedural documentation, although filtering and the internal fine-tuning collection remain underspecified. The code/model access statement is unchanged, and replacement standalone generation examples omit v1's individual prompt captions.

R1.justification: V5 broadens citations and discussion with DreamLLM, Aiello et al., UniD3, Copilot4D, Campbell et al., and the added training-data sources; Wang and Cho's masked-model reference disappears. The basic positioning relative to Chameleon, expert-model combinations, and MaskGIT remains intact.

P1.justification: V5 repairs malformed introductory sentences, adds dedicated Preliminaries and Inference sections and appendices, and relocates the guidance equation into the inference discussion. Most existing prose and the sequence of established sections remain intact, making this a limited reorganization rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V5 adds the diffusion-process schematic and scaling table, expands the attention illustration with a mixed-modality panel, and revises generation, inpainting, sensitivity, and failure-case displays. Table rows and citation formatting also change, and standalone sample prompt captions disappear. These collectively alter the visual exposition substantially; retained figures and the original ablation table are matched across renumbering.

improvement.justification: V5 provides useful scaling evidence in Table 4, broader unified-model comparisons, and clearer decoding instructions in Section 4.4 and Appendix A.2. These support a modest net improvement. Benefits are tempered by underspecified internal training data and errors in the added theory: the backward conditional-independence statement after Equation 3 does not follow from the Markov property, and Equation 5's non-mask rows do not normalize for nonzero beta. Higher scores under expanded training therefore do not establish a major overall quality improvement.
